newsitem.title: USA: Nike stock plunges after it warns about earnings.
newsitem.headline: Nike stock plunges after it warns about earnings.

text.p: Nike Inc. stock plunged by 14 percent Thursday after the company said its fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and income would come in below Wall Street expectations.
Shares of Nike, which had climbed in the previous two days to close at $63.625 Wednesday, fell by $8.875 to $54.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The collapse came after the athletic footware and apparel company said it expected per-share earnings for the three months ending May 31 of between 51 cents and 56 cents -- well below analysts' consensus of 69 cents.
Trading in the stock was halted for about 25 minutes after the NYSE opened to give investors time to digest the news.

Nike, which expects to report its fourth-quarter results in July, said its earnings would be lower primarily because its revenues for the period would fall below analysts' estimates, although it forecast that revenue and earnings for the full year would hit record levels.

The company also said its fourth-quarter earnings would be impacted by a one-time, pre-tax charge of $18 million, or 4 cents a share, primarily related to the shutdown of a manufacturing plant at Bauer Inc., its hockey equipment unit.
The company, which is based in Beaverton, Ore., said the plant shutdown was part of its long-term plan to reposition some manufacturing facilities to more cost-effective overseas operations.

Nike also said its lower estimated revenues were partly attributable "to shifts in the mix of futures and at-once orders, timing of shipments in Europe, product shortages, and a slight increase in U.S. order cancellations."
It did not provide further details.

Nike stock, which has been battered this year by concerns about slowing growth in its core U.S. footwear market, rallied on Tuesday and Wednesday as Wall Street speculated that billionaire investor Warren Buffett favours the company as an investment.

Traders said they believed Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. had used its GEICO insurance company as the vehicle to buy into Nike, which last month hit a recent low of $51.25 a share -- down from more than $76 in February.
